title: Integers
example: −4, 0 and 7 are integers, while ½ is not.
note: Negative whole numbers are integers as well.

title: Rational numbers
parts: x can be written as a ratio of two integers with nonzero denominator.
note: A number with a repeating decimal can still be rational.
wrong: x must have a terminating decimal expansion.

title: Imaginary unit
parts: Squaring the imaginary unit i gives negative one.
note: In a+bi, b is the real coefficient of i.
wrong: Squaring the imaginary unit gives positive one.

title: Arithmetic sequence
parts: The nth term is the first term a plus n−1 copies of the common difference d.
example: If a=4 and d=3, the fourth term is 4+3×3=13.
note: The first term already equals a, so it needs zero steps.
wrong: Add n copies of d to the first term.

title: Sum of an arithmetic series
parts: Multiply the number of terms by the average of the first and last terms.
note: Sₙ is the sum of the terms. Tₙ represents just the nth term.
wrong: Take only the last term of the sequence.

title: Geometric sequence
parts: The nth term is the first term a multiplied by the common ratio r a total of n−1 times.
example: For 2,6,18,… the ratio is 3 and T₄=2×3³=54.
note: The common ratio multiplies each term. Adding the same amount gives an arithmetic sequence.
wrong: Add r to the first term n−1 times.

title: Infinite geometric series
parts: The sum of all terms is a divided by one minus r, when |r|<1.
example: 4+2+1+⋯ has a=4 and r=½, so its sum is 8.
note: The sum formula requires the magnitude of the ratio to be less than one.
wrong: This gives a finite sum for every value of r.

title: Inductive step
parts: Assuming the statement for k, prove it for the next integer k+1.
note: An induction proof also requires a base case.
wrong: Test only the statement P(1), then stop.

title: Negative exponent
parts: A negative exponent gives the reciprocal of the positive power, for nonzero a.
note: A negative exponent does not itself make the result negative.
wrong: Negate the positive power of a.

title: Fractional exponent
parts: For positive a, raise it to one over n by taking its nth root.
note: The denominator of the exponent gives the root index.

title: Scientific notation
parts: Multiply 3.2 by ten to the fourth power.
note: An exponent of −4 would instead move the decimal four places left.

title: Percentage error
parts: Divide absolute error by the magnitude of the nonzero exact value and express it as a percentage.
example: A measurement of 48 instead of 50 gives 100×2/50=4%.
note: Divide by the reference value, rather than by the measured value.
wrong: Divide the error by the measured value and report that percentage.

title: Compound interest
parts: The starting amount P is multiplied by one plus the rate i for each of n periods.
example: €200 at 5% per year for two years grows to 200×1.05²=€220.50.
note: Use 0.05 for a rate of 5%. The rate and period count must use the same time unit.
wrong: Add interest each period on the original amount only.

title: Present value
parts: Discount a future amount A by dividing by the growth factor for n periods.
example: €121 due in two years at 10% per year has present value €121/1.1²=€100.
wrong: Multiply the future amount by the growth factor.

title: Volume of a cylinder
parts: Multiply the area of the circular base by the perpendicular height.
example: Radius 3 cm and height 5 cm give volume 45π cm³.
note: Use the radius, rather than the diameter. Volume is measured in cubic units.
wrong: Multiply the base circumference by the height.

title: Surface area of a sphere
parts: The sphere’s surface area is four times the area of a disc of radius r.
example: For r=2 cm, the surface area is 16π cm².
note: Square units measure area. The volume formula uses r cubed.
